title: Normal And Extensive Perfection Can Differ
body_html:
Normal And Extensive Perfection Can Differ

MFoGT Section 6.6 gives examples showing that normal-form perfection and extensive-form perfection are distinct refinements.

  • In the game of Figure 6.18, the indicated profile is extensive-form perfect but not perfect in the associated normal form.
  • In the game of Figure 6.19, the indicated profile is perfect in the normal form but not perfect in the extensive form.

The text also notes that some games have empty intersection between the two sets of refinements.

References

  • [MFoGT, Section 6.6, Figures 6.18 and 6.19] Laraki, Renault, and Sorin, Mathematical Foundations of Game Theory. Examples where extensive-form perfection and normal-form perfection disagree.
